Resolves #19465

A distinct descendant drag handle now leaves its pane body outside native drag admission. Initial and inserted items use the same protected root-marker predicate, while `isDraggableItem()` continues to own sortable membership. Body text selection, input and scrolling stay native; the marked header still starts sorting. Whole-item mode, the legacy marker selector and root tab-header handles retain their behavior.

Evidence: local native browser gestures and a mutation control cover this Engine leaf. Institution `#601` remains the separate consumer configuration and installed FM acceptance.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; change class is restoration. Repository pre-commit checks passed; final-head Engine/shared baseline jobs run on this PR.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | `HeaderHandleAdmissionNL.spec.mjs` checks native guard absence, non-empty text selection, input clicking/typing and scrolling on initial and inserted panes. |
| AC-2 | The same browser test drives the marked header, verifies real sort engagement and checks guard cleanup after release. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered marker units retain null/default/root-handle modes and authored descendant markers; tab, grid, Mouse/Touch and native HTML drag-source controls pass. |
| AC-4 | Restoring the old two marker decisions makes the permanent browser test fail; [validation receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19465#issuecomment-6051167004). |

## Deltas from ticket

Adds protected `isItemRootDragTarget(item)` at the existing container drag-zone projection boundary. This separates native target marking from sortable membership without adding sensor metadata or a Mouse-only filter. No consumer workaround is removed because the prior consumer configuration could not prevent the early native claim.

## Test Evidence

- Combined popup-return and header-admission browser journeys pass together (2/2); [exact-head integration receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19464#issuecomment-6053798161).
- New browser witness passes on the repair and fails with the original marker decisions restored: a body press activates `neo-drag-active` despite worker refusal.
- Browser compatibility bundle: 10/10 across body interactions, tab-header actions, grid header resize and cross-region column dragging.
- An earlier control removes only the outer marker: body selection returns and the same header still tears out. [Receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19465#issuecomment-6051167004).

- `6e161a45b8` — await the dashboard instance before querying fixture state.

- `f67bdd12c1` — document the native marker requirement for descendant handles.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge** (non-blocking): the root-handle test compares `item.vdom.cls` by exact equality (`includes` / `===`), while `isDraggableItem` matches the same handle through `VDomUtil.find(item.vdom, {cls})`. A root whose `cls` is a space-separated string would be read as a descendant handle and lose its marker. In-tree roots use array `cls`, so nothing hits it today; reusing the `VDomUtil` matcher on the root node would keep the two predicates symmetric.
- **Checked and cleared:** in-tree consumers at `6e161a45b8`: `git grep "dragHandleSelector\s*:"` over `src`, `apps` and `examples` finds exactly `draggable/dashboard/SortZone.mjs:53` (`.neo-draggable`, legacy, stays marked) and `draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs:31` (`.neo-tab-header-button`, root handle, stays marked), so no existing sort changes behavior; both hits are the positive control for the pattern. The sensors admit a press only through `dragTargetClasses` (`sensor/Base.mjs:21-23`), and the NL witness authors `neo-draggable` on its handle (`HeaderHandleAdmissionNL.spec.mjs:20`). The test therefore proves the contract the Required Action asks the docs to state.
